citation: 'Interior court', John J. Glessner House, 1800 South Prairie Avenue, Chicago, photograph circa 1923 from J. J. Glessner, The Story of a House (1923); HABS photocopy, HABS IL-1015 photograph 5 of 17 (call number HABS ILL,16-CHIG,17--5). Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division (HABS). Master TIFF 060907pu.tif in the owner's Internet Archive item master-pnp-habshaer-il-il0100-il0118-photos; 1800 px web copy committed at chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/public/glessner-habs-photo-05.jpg (Prairie library source pa-glessner-habs-photo-05, PR #169).
locator: The whole print: the courtyard looking north-east, from the dining bay (left) past the hall bow and the east wing's courtyard face with its dormers and round stair tower to the underpass exit (right).
rights_note: A HABS copy of a photograph published in 1923; LOC notes that images copied from other sources may be restricted. Cited in text; only measurements and forms are read from it, and nothing is derived from the image as an asset.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-09-28 (T-1732) from the committed 1800 px web copy.
note: The only view of the courtyard faces read by this project, and it is c. 1923 - nineteen years after the scene date - so it dates what it shows to 1923 and is carried to 1904 only for masonry and roof forms nothing records changing (the 1892 changes were interior; the first recorded exterior work is 1946). It shows: the dining bay as a masonry storey with a glazed band over it and a tall faceted metal roof (where the plans alone suggested a one-storey bay); the hall bow two storeys to the eave; three pyramid-roofed dormers and the conical stair tower; the underpass exit; a lawn with a hard carriage drive along the south side; bare vine stems on the tower and the bow.
what_it_supplies: the dining bay's elevation and roof form
the hall bow's height and lights
the courtyard's lawn and drive in c. 1923
confirmation of the dormers and stair tower
